svg.text: SQL basics — Memory: Stack / Heap / Static (high level)
The lesson's own locals only hold SQL text; the tables and rows live outside .NET, inside SQL Server.
Every local is a pointer to a string
inList, balanceRange, startsWithC, oneLetterWildcard, nullEquals, nullIs
One small string object per query
SELECT … FROM Accounts WHERE AccountType = 'Savings' ORDER BY AccountId
the SQL as text; its line breaks are kept
23 query strings across the six methods
each is read by SqlLab, then sent to SQL Server
No rows held by the lesson's locals
SqlLab.Show copies the rows into a temporary list only to print them, then lets it go
your lesson code (the Demo locals) never holds a row
OUTSIDE .NET — SQL Server: the three bank tables BankSeed.Recreate() builds (22 rows in total)
Dana Smith (highlighted) owns no account. Every query reads these rows and changes none of them.
A query is only text until SQL Server runs it. The Heap holds the question; the answer — rows — is printed by SqlLab.Show (which holds them only briefly) and no lesson local keeps them.
The dashed grey box is the recorded "OUTSIDE" addition to the locked 3-column shape (as in Topic 8); Stack, Heap and Static themselves are unchanged. Each Memory/<N> diagram draws it per method.
